clue.text: Huge tunnel blown up with ammo

indicators.note: something blown up is shattered into pieces, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vast tunnel destroyed by explosives, like a demolition scene or a wartime raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The ammunition in the surface is what blows the tunnel up; in the wordplay the ammo is simply more letters to mix in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monumental is enormous in scale, like a great memorial structure, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: He wanted some more cut fruit

indicators.note: a cut name has been trimmed short, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: Oliver Twist, the Dickens orphan who famously asked for more gruel

explanation.surface: Someone hungry for more fruit, so the fruit gets chopped up for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous line 'Please, sir, I want some more' belongs to Oliver Twist in Dickens's novel; dropping the last R leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An olive is the small oily stone fruit of the olive tree, eaten whole or pressed for oil.

clue.text: Account ruthlessly suppresses falsehood

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep something held down out of sight, so the answer sits concealed inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A financial report that brutally covers up a lie, like a dishonest company audit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' looks like the definition of something bookish; it only supplies the tail letters UNT before RUTH from the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a lie, a statement that is not true, which is exactly a falsehood.

clue.text: Regularly nervier the day before a festival

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who gets more anxious each time a big celebration approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of 'nervier' gives E, V, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve name the evening or day immediately preceding a holiday.

clue.text: Persistent chartered accountant after tax returns and debtor's notes

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: income after tax is net
CA stands for chartered accountant
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A dogged accountant chasing tax returns and unpaid IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: Net income is what remains after tax, which is how 'tax' leads there; 'returns' turns round both short pieces in place before the debtor's notes follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenacious person holds firmly to a purpose and refuses to give up, the same as persistent.

clue.text: Unit set fire to centre of forest

parts.note: to light a fire is to set it, past tense lit

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the innermost letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two of six letters

explanation.surface: A military unit torching the heart of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' suggests soldiers in the surface, but it is a unit of measure; 'set fire to' reads as one phrase, while only 'set fire' gives LIT and 'to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is the metric unit of volume, a thousand cubic centimetres.

clue.text: Servant returned company artwork

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a serf was a feudal labourer bound to a lord
the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A servant giving back a painting that belonged to a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the servant is turned round; the company abbreviation follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling, a classic form of art.

clue.text: Walk quietly from edge to edge of edge

parts.note: a tip is an end or edge
taken as written

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its outer border, here its very first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Creeping silently along a ledge, side to side, like someone on a narrow parapet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From edge to edge' reads as a direction across, but the first edge is a synonym, 'to' stays as itself, and the last edge gives just its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to move on the balls of the feet so as to make no noise.

clue.text: Break tea urn in temper

indicators.note: something broken falls apart into pieces that can be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone smashing the office tea urn in a fit of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' in the surface is anger; as the definition it means a person's disposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's temper in the older sense is their character or disposition, which is their nature.

clue.text: Starts to play energetic sport for country

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Taking up a vigorous game on behalf of one's nation.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, rugby union, is the standard crossword sport; it follows the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation on the Pacific coast, an example of a country.

clue.text: Ancient civilisation taking on European expansion

indicators.note: to take something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the pre-Columbian people of the Andes
on, in the sense of about or concerning
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An old empire absorbing European ways as it grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking on' looks like one phrase meaning adopting, but 'on' is RE (as in a memo's subject line) and is what the Incas take in.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a growth in size or amount, which is what expansion means.

clue.text: Bring in social worker of influence

parts.note: to bring goods into a country
the ant is a social insect and a worker of its colony

explanation.surface: Hiring a powerful social worker to sort out a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a caseworker but an insect: ants live in colonies, and the sterile ones are called workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of influence carries weight and matters, which is what important describes.

clue.text: Clergyman who might be seen on board?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a senior priest in charge of a diocese

definitions.text: who might be seen on board
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a chess piece, found on the chessboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship or a committee; the board is a chessboard, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a high-ranking church officer and the chess piece that moves diagonally.

clue.text: A biro's broken making line on chart

indicators.note: a broken thing comes apart, letting the letters be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ballpoint pen leaking and leaving a stray stroke across a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: A biro is a ballpoint pen; the 's counts as a letter in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Choice of mixing up elixir's first two ingredients

indicators.note: mixing things up puts them into a different order

parts.note: an elixir is a magic drink; only its first two letters, its 'ingredients', are swapped

explanation.surface: Deciding which way to blend the first two components of a magic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters of the elixir are swapped; 'ingredients' plays on the drink and stands for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one thing you may pick from several alternatives, so it is a choice.

clue.text: Hard-bitten drill-sergeant clutches strand of hair

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tightly, so the answer is gripped within the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A tough drill instructor grabbing a recruit by a lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the hyphenated words: the end of 'bitten' and the start of 'drill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender curling wisp, used of hair as well as of the shoots that climbing plants coil.

clue.text: Notes similarity of hosts for the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so this is a word that is heard rather than seen

parts.note: comperes are the hosts of shows

explanation.surface: Observing that the presenters of a show are rather alike, as the audience watches.
explanation.walkthrough: A compere is the master of ceremonies at a show, a mostly British word; the two spellings are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare things is to note how they resemble each other, so it matches noting a likeness.

clue.text: Shape public relations ideology

parts.note: standard abbreviation
an ism is any doctrine or belief system

explanation.surface: Spin doctors moulding a political ideology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shape' reads as a verb meaning to mould; it is the noun naming a solid figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a solid geometric figure with two identical end faces and flat sides, a three-dimensional form.

clue.text: Feature in techno session

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the next words, hidden across them

parts.note: the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A spot on a techno music recording session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests a newspaper or radio piece about the session; it is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is one of the parts of the face, which are known as features.

clue.text: Pack contains four of these outfits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a deck of cards has four groups, hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades
second meaning: matching jacket and trouser sets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' suggests luggage, as if packing clothes; it is a pack of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the four card groups in a deck and formal sets of clothes worn together.

clue.text: Mail runs entertaining article in paper

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one piece holds another
running colours bleed and shift, so the letters move out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper called the Mail running a feature article, a nod to the puzzle's own Globe and Mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' and 'paper' look like one subject, a newspaper; the mail letters are rearranged, then wrap around the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is a strong buff paper, originally made from hemp, used for envelopes and folders.

clue.text: Quickly pull on fashionable jacket

parts.note: a jerk is a sudden sharp tug
in fashion

explanation.surface: Hurriedly throwing on a trendy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull on' reads as putting on clothes, but 'on' belongs to neither half; 'Quickly pull' is the tug and 'on' merely joins it to the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, historically of leather.

clue.text: Work book

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a task or employment
second meaning: a book of the Old Testament

explanation.walkthrough: 'Work book' looks like a single school exercise book; split, each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means paid employment and is also the name of the Old Testament book about a much-tested man.

clue.text: Doctor omits blame in process

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician who avoids pointing the finger during some procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, a physician; it is the verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the chemical process by which a living body turns food into energy.
